structural_issues: The analogy implies permanent alteration of content (reprinted books, audiobooks), while most assistive technologies act as reversible overlays.
Elevator-to-switch control mapping conflates physical relocation with an alternative input mechanism, weakening structural correspondence.
Magnifying glass leading to permanent larger print differs from temporary, user‑controlled screen magnification.
result.rationale: Two of the three mappings align well with the target concepts, but the elevator‑switch control correspondence and the permanent‑change implication introduce logical stretches.
